oil.summary: Crude markets split sharply today: Brent surged 3.27% to $109.33/bbl, extending its weekly gain to +4.45%, while WTI added a more modest +0.71% to $98.62/bbl. The Brent/WTI spread blowout reflects Hormuz risk premium as Iran intensifies tanker attacks and oil flows through the strait plummet. Ukraine's strike on the Ryazan refinery and the collapse of the US-brokered Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire added fresh supply-disruption anxiety. Distillates diverged from crude: RBOB fell 1.64% and heating oil shed 2.85% on the day, likely reflecting a US-Russia diesel deal that eased near-term product supply fears. Options markets remain firmly biased toward an OPEC cut at the next meeting (77.26% probability). Trump faces a 10-day deadline on 100% tariffs for Russian oil buyers, adding a further policy wildcard.
drivers: Iran intensifying Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks, sharply curtailing Gulf oil flows and lifting Brent risk premium
Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire breakdown and Ukrainian strike on Ryazan refinery reinforce upstream supply disruption concerns
US-Russia diesel deal and Trump's 10-day tariff decision on Russian oil buyers inject product-market and policy uncertainty

gas.summary: Henry Hub slipped 2.84% to $3.145/MMBtu, extending a weekly loss of 2.36%, while TTF eased 0.81% to €86.432/MWh after a blistering +9.62% weekly rally. The Atlantic divergence persists: European prices remain structurally elevated as the Iran war-driven LNG supply crunch squeezes Middle Eastern deliveries, turning Europe's residual coal capacity profitable and forcing two German power retailers out of business. South Korea has similarly pivoted back to coal as spot LNG premiums bite. China's early stockpiling ahead of winter offers a partial demand offset and may limit further Asian spot LNG price escalation. Zelensky warned a US-Russia gas deal could follow the diesel pact, introducing a tail risk that could eventually loosen European supply.
drivers: Iran war-driven Middle Eastern LNG disruption sustaining elevated TTF and triggering coal-to-gas switching reversals in Europe and South Korea
China's pre-built winter gas inventories may cap extreme Asian spot LNG demand, providing marginal supply relief
Potential US-Russia gas deal flagged by Zelensky represents a downside price risk if ceasefire diplomacy resurfaces

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) slipped 2.16% to $80.92/EUA, drifting slightly lower on the week (-1.95%) despite the LNG crunch that is driving coal-fired generation back into dispatch across Europe and South Korea. The carbon price weakness is notable given the surge in coal burn — two German power retailers have already failed under spiking wholesale prices. Russia's 39-ballistic-missile strike on Ukraine's power grid earlier this week left 600,000 people without electricity and drew Zelensky's charge that Moscow violated Trump's own ceasefire framework. Data-centre-led renewable demand growth in India represents a structural demand tailwind for clean power investment but is a longer-dated signal. Near-term, the power complex is dominated by the gas price squeeze and war-related grid disruptions.
drivers: Russia's ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's power grid undermining ceasefire credibility and heightening European energy security anxiety
LNG supply crunch restoring profitability to European coal-fired power while pushing two German electricity retailers into insolvency
EUA carbon price softening despite rising coal burn, creating a potential dislocation to watch if coal dispatch data confirms a sustained ramp
